ceo_directive: Define regulatory pathway: device classification, combination product rules, CNS-contact material requirements
invention: A1_MODIFIED: ePTFE size-selective membrane + pressure-relief bypass integrated into eShunt

base_eshunt_classification.product_code: PMA, existing eShunt PMA assumed via STRIDE
base_eshunt_classification.rationale: The base eShunt is a permanently implantable CSF diversion device. Permanent CNS implants are Class III by FDA panel precedent (shunts, ICP monitors, drug pumps).

a1_modified_classification.rationale: Adding an intraluminal membrane does not downgrade the device; it adds a device-side feature that contacts CSF and may retain a therapeutic. Class III still required.

combination_product_designation.type: Device/Biologic (if used with gene therapy vector such as scAAV9) or Device/Drug (if used with small molecule or biologic therapeutic)
combination_product_designation.lead_center_assumption: CDRH-led (because primary mode of action is mechanical CSF drainage, not drug delivery)
combination_product_designation.consult_center: CDER (small molecule) or CBER (biologic/gene therapy vector)
combination_product_designation.legal_basis: 21 CFR 3.4 — primary mode of action determines lead center; device is the primary mode here because drainage must occur for any therapeutic effect.
combination_product_designation.opa_application_step: Submit Request for Designation (RFD) to FDA OOPD early, before pre-submission

predicate_analysis.rationale: Existing predicates (Codman Certas, Medtronic Programmable, Sophysa Polaris) are CSF shunts WITHOUT intraluminal drug-retention membranes. No valid predicate for the new membrane-retention feature. 510(k) path foreclosed; PMA supplement or new PMA required.

pma_supplement_viability.applicable_if: CereVasc already holds PMA for base eShunt at time of A1 modification
pma_supplement_viability.supplement_type: Panel-track or 180-day supplement depending on contact-time and material change
pma_supplement_viability.rationale: Adding a permanent intraluminal membrane in contact with CSF is a significant modification (new material contacting CNS, new mechanism of action). 180-day supplement most likely required.

iso_10993_subset_applicable.required_tests: Categorization 5 (implant devices, tissue/bone/dentin) AND Categorization 11 (circulating blood)

iso_10993_subset_applicable.rationale: Direct cytotoxicity of membrane material and any extractables on neural/glial cell lines.

iso_10993_subset_applicable.scope: Tests for local effects after implantation
iso_10993_subset_applicable.rationale: Implant membrane in subarachnoid space model; assess local neuroinflammatory response.
Membrane extractables could enter CSF and bloodstream.
Full extractables/leachables profile for membrane + bypass sleeve.
Supplementary to -10 for neural tissue response.

cns_contact_material_requirements.usp_class_vi: Recommended for membrane substrate (ePTFE already meets this in vascular indications)
fda_specific_guidance_documents: Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff: Class II Special Controls Guidance Document for CSF Shunts (where applicable to supplement)
Guidance for Industry: Preparation of IDEs and INDs for Combination Products
Use of International Standard ISO 10993-1 (FDA 2016 / 2020 update)
Guidance for Industry: Considerations for the Use of Carcinogenicity Studies — generally not required for shunt materials but considered for novel polymer membranes in permanent CNS contact

neurotoxicity_testing.rationale: CNS-contacting materials require dedicated neurotoxicity panel beyond standard ISO 10993 series; FDA may require in vitro blood-brain-barrier model + glial activation assay + neuronal viability assay.
models_suggested: In vitro BBB transwell model (hCMEC/D3 + hAstrocyte co-culture)
In vivo chronic subarachnoid implant in ovine or porcine model (6-month minimum)

combination_product_pathway.opa_rfd_timing: Pre-pre-submission (Q-Sub Type B meeting) — file at least 90 days before intended Q-Sub
opa_rfd_inputs: Mode of action statement for both device and drug/biologic
Proposed lead center (CDRH if drainage primary)
Therapeutic agent class (small molecule vs biologic vs gene therapy vector)
Whether therapeutic is already FDA-approved (affects bridging requirements)
combination_product_pathway.expected_designation: DEVICE-LED combination product, CDRH lead, CDER/CBER consult
implications: Single PMA application is acceptable; CDRH is primary reviewer
CDER/CBER consult review of drug-retention claims
If therapeutic is gene therapy vector (e.g., scAAV9), CBER will be heavily involved and may require IND parallel to IDE
Clinical protocol must be designed to isolate device-drainage endpoint from drug-efficacy endpoint

clinical_trial_pathway.ide_submission: FDA Form 3674 + supplements; submit to CDRH PNB
clinical_trial_pathway.ide_phase_1_fpkas: First-in-human safety study in small cohort (n=5-10)
clinical_trial_pathway.pivotal_trial_assumption: Randomized controlled trial vs standard eShunt without A1 modification, n=100-200

endpoints.primary_safety: ICP events, membrane occlusion requiring revision, neurotoxicity
endpoints.primary_performance: Therapeutic agent residence time (CSF sampling) + CSF drainage (ICP control)
endpoints.secondary_efficacy: Depends on therapeutic paired (e.g., NPH symptom score if treating NPH)

expected_duration_to_pma_decision.rationale: Combination product review is slower than device-only PMA. STRIDE precedent (CereVasc base) took ~5 years; A1 modification adds drug/retention complexity.

regulatory_risks.risk: FDA may re-classify as DRUG-LED if retention is deemed the primary mode of action
regulatory_risks.rationale: Without drainage, the device provides no therapeutic benefit. Drainage is necessary and sufficient for CSF volume control; the membrane is a feature, not a separate product. Still, RFD output must be obtained in writing.
regulatory_risks.mitigation: File RFD early; obtain written OOPD designation letter before Q-Sub.

regulatory_risks.risk: Therapeutic agent change forces new PMA supplement per drug class
regulatory_risks.rationale: Each new therapeutic (small molecule vs biologic vs vector) likely requires biocompatibility and efficacy re-testing. The membrane is generic but the retention claim is therapeutic-specific.
regulatory_risks.mitigation: Draft master PMA framework with modular supplements per therapeutic; negotiate with CDRH whether a single PMA can hold multiple therapeutic-specific Indications for Use.

regulatory_risks.risk: ISO 10993-18 extractables exceed thresholds for chronic CNS contact
regulatory_risks.rationale: ePTFE is well-characterized for vascular but its CNS-contact extractables profile is less established. Track-etched polycarbonate is even less characterized for CNS.
regulatory_risks.mitigation: Switch candidate selection (ePTFE > track-etched polycarbonate) for biocompatibility data depth; perform early extractables screen.

regulatory_risks.risk: Membrane occlusion requires revision surgery (Class III recall exposure)
regulatory_risks.rationale: If chronic CSF fouling causes occlusion, the A1 device requires explantation. This is a long-term device reliability risk.
regulatory_risks.mitigation: Pressure-relief bypass valve (already in A1_MODIFIED) reduces ICP emergency but does not eliminate need for revision; engineering test must demonstrate 12-month patency minimum.

regulatory_gate_score.rationale: Pathway is clear (PMA supplement + combination product RFD), but no predicate exists for the retention feature and combination product review adds 12-24 months to a base PMA timeline. Material biocompatibility for ePTFE in vascular is well-established; for CNS contact, additional ISO 10993-6/-11/-18 testing required.

primary_source_provenance.prior_pma_precedent: STRIDE trial (CereVasc eShunt base) — assumed approved; if not yet approved, base PMA must precede A1 supplement.
model_derived_elements: PMA-supplement-vs-new-PMA decision (depends on CereVasc PMA status at time of A1 filing)
OOPD designation outcome (likely CDRH-led but not guaranteed)
